verified.catalyst: Shareholder-approved two-part breakup — CommerceOne acquires Green Dot Bank (GDOT holders receive $8.11 cash + 0.2215 New CommerceOne shares) while Smith Ventures buys the non-bank Payments business for $690M — now gated solely on Federal Reserve, Alabama State Banking Department and Utah DFI approvals, targeted to close Q3 2026.
verified.dated_milestone: Fed/Alabama/Utah bank-regulator approvals then closing, targeted by 2026-09-30 (Q3 2026); no approval announced as of 2026-07-20. Prior dated step: shareholder votes passed 2026-06-23 (99%+ GDOT, 100% CommerceOne).
verified.instrument: common equity (long GDOT vs. deal terms; no listed hedge for the New CommerceOne stub since it is not yet publicly traded)
verified.bloom_gates: G1 + G2 + G3. G1: named counterparties CommerceOne Financial Corp. and Smith Ventures, LLC. G2: definitive, shareholder-approved merger agreement with fixed consideration ($8.11 cash + 0.2215 New CommerceOne shares) and a $690M signed Payments-business sale. G3: the stock leg is a specific currently-unpriced figure — company's illustrative stock value is $6.12-$11.07/share (total $14.23-$19.18), and at $13.40 the market implies roughly $5.29 for the stub, below the low end of the sponsor's own range.
verified.edge: M — the spread is real and mechanically identifiable (price below even the low end of the illustrative consideration range), but the entire discount sits in an unlisted, unmarkable New CommerceOne stub, so "cheap" is not provable without independently underwriting a private Alabama bank holdco. Bank-regulator gating is also the slowest, least handicappable approval path, and Q3 is a target not a covenant.
verified.primary_source: Green Dot/CommerceOne joint press release and GDOT Form 8-K, 2026-06-23 (businesswire.com/news/home/20260623102044; sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1386278/000114036126026125/ef20076604_ex99-1.htm); terms from DEFM14A / 424B3 (SEC, 2026) and the 2025-11-23 announcement release; price from FMP quote 2026-07-20 ($13.40).
verified.kill_fact: Kill attempt FAILED on the event itself — all load-bearing facts verified primary: $8.11 cash + 0.2215 New CommerceOne shares, Smith Ventures $690M for the non-bank Payments business (of which $470M to holders, $155M into the bank, $65M debt paydown), both shareholder bases approved 2026-06-23 (>99% GDOT / 100% CommerceOne), and the ONLY outstanding gates are the Federal Reserve, Alabama State Banking Dept and Utah DFI with a Q3 2026 target — no approval announced as of 2026-07-20, so the event is genuinely forward and un-fired. Live quote confirms $13.40 exactly. TWO CORRECTIONS: (1) The line mischaracterizes the $14.23-$19.18 band as "the sponsor's" valuation implying a $6.12-$11.07 stub floor. It is not a sponsor mark — the DEFM14A/425 states it is an ILLUSTRATIVE sensitivity at an assumed ~1.00x-1.80x tangible book value multiple. The LOW end already assumes 1.0x TBV, so there is no floor at all: an unlisted small-cap bank holdco can and often does open below 1.0x TBV, meaning $13.40 is not provably a discount to intrinsic — the entire gap is an unpriceable stub-multiple bet, which is weaker than the "arb" framing. (2) Timing risk is understated: the close target has ALREADY slipped once, from the Q2 2026 guided at the November 2025 announcement to the current Q3 2026 — the slip the line treats as a hypothetical risk has already happened, and only ~10 weeks of Q3 remain with three separate regulators outstanding. Tradeability is otherwise clean (NYSE, ~$760M cap, ~250k shares/day) and the line honestly self-discloses the un-hedgeable stub leg. Score trimmed 7 to 6 for the illusory floor and the demonstrated timeline slippage.
verified.analysis: This is a genuine, dated, forward, regulator-gated arb rather than a narrative: the definitive agreement is signed, both shareholder bases voted it through on 2026-06-23, and the only remaining gates are Fed, Alabama State Banking Department and Utah DFI approval with a Q3 2026 close target — none of which had been announced as granted by 2026-07-20, so the event has not fired and the spread has not re-rated. At $13.40 the stock trades below even the low end of the company's own $14.23-$19.18 illustrative consideration range, implying roughly $5.29 for the 0.2215 New CommerceOne shares versus the sponsor's $6.12-$11.07; the discount is entirely a stub-valuation and approval-timing question, not a macro bet. Score is capped at 7 rather than higher because the un-hedgeable, unlisted stock leg means the arb cannot be locked and bank-regulator timelines routinely slip past a stated quarter, so the realistic near-term payoff is the modest convergence to roughly $14.50-$15, not the headline high end.

verified.catalyst: Greenfire will launch a rights offering in August 2026 for at least C$575M to repay the bridge loan funding its C$1.277B all-cash acquisition of Connacher Oil and Gas, with Waterous Energy Fund (~72% holder) backstopping the entire raise.
verified.dated_milestone: Rights offering launch and Connacher closing both expected August 2026 (announced July 13, 2026); record date, final subscription price and ratio still "to be determined" — next hard date is the offering circular / record-date announcement, expected within weeks.
verified.instrument: Common equity only (NYSE/TSX dual-listed, ~$460M market cap, thin volume ~312k shares; no usable listed options chain for a position of this type)
verified.bloom_gates: G1 and G2 pass; G3 fails. G1: named counterparties — Waterous Energy Fund (standby purchaser) and Connacher Oil and Gas (target). G2: concrete commitments — definitive C$1.277B cash purchase agreement, new C$575M bridge facility, WEF standby purchase commitment of at least C$575M with full exercise of basic subscription privilege plus all unsubscribed shares. G3 fails: the pro-forma figures (34,000 bbl/d 2026 production vs 19,500 standalone Connacher, 850 mmbbl 2P vs 441 mmbbl) were disclosed with the June/July deal announcements and the stock has already run to 6.35 against a 5.81 50-day and a 7.02 52-week high, so there is no specific currently-unpriced number.
verified.edge: L — the structure is real and dated, but the asymmetry sits with the controller, not the minority. A backstopped rights offering raising more than the entire pre-deal equity value is a cash call, not a value unlock: a minority holder either writes a large cheque to stand still, or is diluted at a 15% discount by a holder already at 72%, mechanically creeping toward squeeze-out territory. The 2024-era strategic review is still nominally open but has produced nothing in eighteen months and is not an independent source of edge. Residual exposure is also a levered WCS/heavy-differential bet, which is close to a macro position.
verified.primary_source: Greenfire Resources news release, "Greenfire Resources Announces Intention to Conduct Rights Offering," July 13, 2026 (greenfireres.com; PDF Greenfire-Resources-Announcement-of-Rights-Offering-20260713.pdf), corroborated by BOE Report July 13, 2026 and the earlier Connacher acquisition release; FMP quote 2026-07-20 (6.35, mkt cap $460M).
verified.analysis: The dated forward event is genuine and specific: an August 2026 rights offering of at least C$575M, fully backstopped by Waterous Energy Fund, whose completion is a closing condition for the C$1.277B Connacher acquisition — so the milestone is structural, not narrative, and has not yet fired. But the trade fails on skew rather than on fact. The raise exceeds Greenfire's entire ~$460M pre-deal equity value, and the backstop hands every unsubscribed share to a holder already at ~72% at a 15% discount, meaning the minority's realistic outcomes are "pay up to stand still" or "be diluted at a controller-set price" — the controller owns the option, and terms that matter most (record date, final price, ratio, any minority protections) are still undetermined. Holding at WATCH/5 rather than promoting: revisit when the offering circular fixes the record date and subscription terms, which is the point at which minority treatment becomes assessable; the gap in this verification is that no circular exists yet, so the actual dilution math cannot be computed.

verified.analysis: The underlying event is genuine and forward -- GRAIL filed the final PMA module on 29 Jan 2026 and the FDA has not ruled -- but it fails the DATED gate outright: device PMAs carry no public action date, no advisory committee has been noticed in the Federal Register, and the only public guidance is an analyst-level "late 2026 or early 2027," a window wide enough to make this a position rather than a catalyst. It also fails on pricing: at $72.62 the shares sit up ~142% from the $29.95 52-wk low with a $3.1B cap on a pre-approval, pre-reimbursement diagnostic, so approval optionality is substantially embedded, while the residual downside (CRL or an adverse AdCom on MCED specificity/overdiagnosis, the exact issues FDA panels have flagged for this class) is not. Verification gap: I could not confirm from the Q2-2026 call whether management has narrowed the review timeline or disclosed an FDA filing-acceptance date, which is the one datum that could re-date this -- if an AdCom is later noticed in the Federal Register, this should be re-triaged immediately as a genuinely dated binary.
